title: EU AI Act Article 59 Post-Market Monitoring — What High-Risk Providers Must Report and When
context: 2026-08-27 engine cycle — Article 59 post-market monitoring obligations are now in force; this seed answers the top provider question about reporting thresholds and evidential standards
body: Article 59 of the EU AI Act requires providers of high-risk AI systems to establish and document a post-market monitoring (PMM) system that is proportionate to the nature of the AI system and the risks it presents. The obligation is operational, not aspirational: providers must actively collect, document, and analyse data on the performance of high-risk AI systems throughout their lifetime, and they must report any serious incident or malfunctioning to the relevant market surveillance authority without undue delay — and in any event within 15 days of becoming aware of it. The PMM system must cover at minimum: (1) a systematic method for collecting relevant data from users or other sources on the system's performance; (2) a documented procedure for evaluating whether the system continues to meet the essential requirements of the AI Act; (3) a mechanism for recording and investigating incidents and near-misses; and (4) a process for determining whether a corrective action or market withdrawal is necessary. The Council of AI's posture is monitored containment, not provable isolation: the PMM obligation does not require proof that the system will never fail — it requires a documented, continuously operating evidence trail showing that the provider is actively monitoring, capable of detecting degradation, and responds with recorded corrective actions. A provider preparing for Article 59 compliance should (a) instrument their AI system to produce structured, machine-readable performance logs; (b) maintain a PMM plan as a living document that is updated with each monitoring cycle; and (c) ensure each monitoring record and incident report carries a verified measurement credential — a signed, auditable assertion that the monitoring record was created at the claimed time with the claimed data and has not been altered since. Providers that can produce independently verifiable PMM evidence on demand will be in the strongest position as market surveillance authorities begin systematic audits in late 2026.
